_comment: Balance catalogue: the values and rules the public Game values page shows, and the extra values the plugin watches. Notes and rules were drafted from cvar help text, plugin sources and server.so, and published by the owner on 2026-09-25. Vanilla values for game cvars are the engine defaults read from a local L4D1 dedicated server; plugin cvars have none.

values.label: Survivors per team
values.note: Players on the survivor team.

values.label: Incaps before black and white
values.note: Times you can go down and be picked up before the next incap kills you. On your last life the screen goes black and white.

values.label: Revive time
values.note: How long picking up a downed or hanging teammate takes.

values.label: Health after a revive
values.note: Temporary health you get back when picked up. It drains over time like pill health.

values.label: Ledge hang health
values.note: Health while hanging from a ledge. Hitting 0 drops you.

values.label: Temporary health decay
values.note: How fast temporary health from pills and revives drains away.

values.label: Shotgun reserve ammo
values.note: Spare shells you can carry for either shotgun, on top of the loaded ones.

values.label: Uzi reserve ammo
values.note: Spare Uzi bullets you can carry, on top of the magazine.

values.label: Uzi reload: magazine counts after
values.note: CS:GO style reload: once this much of the reload has passed the new magazine is in, so you can switch away and keep it.

values.label: Uzi reload animation length
values.note: Length of the full Uzi reload. 0 means the game's own length.

values.label: Pistol reload: magazine counts after
values.note: CS:GO style reload for a single pistol, 30% longer while you are down.

values.label: Dual pistol reload: magazine counts after
values.note: Same for dual pistols.

values.label: Shove fatigue
values.note: Extra shove fatigue each shove adds while you are not yet fatigued, so spamming shove tires you out sooner.

values.label: Friendly shoves push teammates
values.note: Whether a shove pushes a teammate. 0 means shoving a teammate does nothing.

values.label: Gravity
values.note: World gravity for everyone. Lower means higher, longer jumps and pounces.

values.label: Common infected limit
values.note: Most common infected alive at once, hordes included. A plugin removes any common beyond this + 5. Set by l4dready when the round goes live.

values.label: Panic event horde size
values.note: How many commons a panic event (alarm, crescendo, finale wave) sends in total. Never more than the common limit + 5 are alive at once, extras are removed as they spawn. Set by l4dready when the round goes live.

values.label: Bonus per unused pills
values.note: Added to a survivor's health bonus for pills still held at the saferoom, even if they are down.

values.label: Natural hordes off
values.note: 1 means the game never sends hordes on a timer. Hordes then come only from panic events (alarms, crescendos, finales), boomer bile and the anti-bait countdown. Rotoblin keeps this at 1.

values.label: Anti-bait: infected up for
values.note: The anti-bait countdown can only start once every infected player has been up (spawned or ghost) this long.

values.label: Anti-bait horde timer
values.note: Countdown, once started, before two hordes are sent at survivors who are still not moving.

values.label: Anti-bait: progress that counts as moving
values.note: Share of the map survivors must cover to reset the anti-bait countdown.

values.label: Commons fighting each other
values.note: Chance that wandering commons who bump into each other start fighting.

values.label: Car alarm trigger distance
values.note: Distance setting for car alarms going off.

values.label: Tank health
values.note: Versus multiplies this by the tank health multiplier below. Vanilla versus is 4000 x 1.5 = 6000.

values.label: Tank versus health multiplier
values.note: Versus tank health is the tank health above times this. 1 means no bonus.

values.label: Tank speed (versus)
values.note: Tank running speed in versus. Survivors run at 220.

values.label: Time for fire to kill a tank
values.note: A lit tank burns to death in this time whatever its health, unless a burn cap is on. Molotovs and gas cans are removed in our PUG mode, so this mostly matters in Lite.

values.label: Tank burn damage cap
values.note: Most fire damage a tank can take in one round before the fire goes out. 0 means off: fire burns the tank to death. Molotovs and gas cans are removed in our PUG mode, so this mostly matters in Lite.

values.label: Frustration: grace after spawning
values.note: The frustration meter does not fill for this long after the tank spawns.

values.label: Frustration: time without sight
values.note: The frustration meter only fills after the tank has gone this long without seeing a survivor.

values.label: Ground pound time
values.note: How long the tank is locked in its swing at a survivor who is down.

values.label: Rotoblin tank rotation off
values.note: 1 means the game's own random lottery picks the tank player, as in vanilla. 0 switches on Rotoblin's rotation, where every infected player takes a turn.

values.label: Witch health
values.note: Witch health.

values.label: Witch speed
values.note: How fast a startled witch runs.

values.label: Witch anger rate
values.note: How fast the witch gets angry when survivors are near, shine a light on her or shoot near her. Higher startles her sooner.

values.label: Witch personal space
values.note: Survivors inside this distance make the witch angry just by being there.

values.label: Witch flashlight range
values.note: A flashlight shone on the witch from within this distance makes her angry.

values.label: Witch damage per hit
values.note: Damage a witch slash does to a survivor who is already down.

values.label: Witch unstuck mode
values.note: Our fix for witches that freeze on a corner mid-chase. 0 off, 1 logs only, 2 moves her past the snag.

values.label: Pounce damage
values.note: Damage each pounce tick does to a pinned survivor.

values.label: Pounce damage interval
values.note: Time between those pounce damage ticks.

values.label: Damage to interrupt a pounce (skeet)
values.note: Damage a hunter must take in the air to be knocked out of a pounce, the skeet.

values.label: Maximum DP (damage pounce) damage
values.note: Most damage a pounce can do on landing, including the base. Also moves the full damage distance.

values.label: Maximum pounce bonus damage
values.note: Extra damage a full distance pounce adds on top of the base. Set by the max DP damage plugin to one less than the max.

values.label: Pounce stumble radius
values.note: Survivors this close to a pounce landing stumble. 0 means only the victim is hit.

values.label: Hunter scratch damage
values.note: Damage of a hunter's scratch when not pouncing.

values.label: Shove angle vs hunter
values.note: How wide a cone a shove covers against a hunter. Wider is easier to deadstop.

values.label: Shove angle vs pouncing hunter
values.note: Shove cone against a hunter mid-pounce. 0 also switches on the no-deadstop rule below.

values.label: Lunge stagger time
values.note: How long a pounce that hits a survivor but does not pin them staggers them.

values.label: Pounce damage to doors
values.note: Damage a pounce does to a door it hits.

values.label: Wallkicks blocked
values.note: 1 blocks hunter wallkicks, 0 allows them.

values.label: Sky pounce fix on
values.note: Our limit on hunters pouncing off the sky ceiling for extra height and distance.

values.label: Sky pounce fix mode
values.note: 1 copies Zen's rule (a pounce started at the ceiling-skimming angle gets a short no-attack time). 2 limits only pounces that push off the sky.

values.label: Tongue cooldown
values.note: Cooldown after a pull, counted from the moment the smoker lets go.

values.label: Damage to break a tongue
values.note: Damage the smoker must take during a pull to let go. A high value means you have to kill him.

values.label: Choke damage
values.note: Damage each choke tick does while the smoker holds a survivor in place.

values.label: Choke damage interval
values.note: Time between choke ticks.

values.label: Drag damage
values.note: Damage of each drag hit after the first. A plugin deals it, so the game setting reads 0 and the live value is not shown.

values.label: First drag damage
values.note: Damage of the first drag hit.

values.label: First drag damage delay
values.note: Time from the grab to the first drag hit.

values.label: Drag damage interval
values.note: Time between drag hits after the first.

values.label: Shove fatigue after a tongue release
values.note: Shove fatigue given to a survivor as the tongue lets go, to slow them down. 0 means none.

values.label: Smokers per team
values.note: Most smokers the infected team can have alive at once. QuadCaps can lower it for one wave after a boomer dies.

values.label: Vomit cooldown
values.note: Cooldown between vomits.

values.label: Vomit range
values.note: How far the vomit reaches.

values.label: Shoves to pop a boomer (min)
values.note: Fewest shoves that pop a boomer.

values.label: Shoves to pop a boomer (max)
values.note: Most shoves it can take before popping.

values.label: Boomers per team
values.note: Most boomers the infected team can have alive at once. QuadCaps lowers it for one wave after a boomer dies.

values.label: Infected players
values.note: Players on the infected team.

values.label: Spawn timer (min)
values.note: Shortest respawn timer after dying.

values.label: Spawn timer (max)
values.note: Longest respawn timer after dying.

values.label: Minimum ghost spawn delay
values.note: Shortest time a ghost must wait before it can spawn.

values.label: Respawn interval
values.note: The game's own wording: infected can try a respawn within this many seconds of spawning.

values.label: Maximum stagger time
values.note: Longest a shoved special infected staggers. Boomers are the exception: they stagger for about 3 s, because the plugin that caps them is switched off together with gravity stagger.

values.label: Door damage per hit
values.note: Damage an infected claw does to a door.

values.label: Chance the wave after a last boomer is 3 hunters + 1 smoker
values.note: Chance the wave after a boomer dies last is 3 hunters and a smoker instead of 4 hunters.

values.label: Health item style
values.note: Where health items come from. 0 map default, 1 kits become pills, 2 same but finale kits stay, 3 finale kits become pills and every other pill or kit is removed, 4 kits become pills and only saferoom kits are removed.

values.label: Weapon style
values.note: 1 replaces rifles with Uzis and auto shotguns with pump shotguns. Hunting rifles stay on the map, see the limit below.

values.label: Throwables on
values.note: 1 leaves pipe bombs and molotovs on the map, 0 removes them.

values.label: Gas cans and propane on
values.note: 1 leaves gas cans, propane and oxygen tanks on the map, 0 removes them.

values.label: Pump shotgun limit
values.note: Most pump shotguns the survivor team can hold at once. -1 means no limit.

values.label: Uzi limit
values.note: Most Uzis the survivor team can hold at once. -1 means no limit.

values.label: Hunting rifle limit
values.note: Most hunting rifles the survivor team can hold at once. 0 means they sit on the map but cannot be picked up.

values.label: Pistol density
values.note: How many spare pistols the game places across the map.

values.label: Boss spawn flow (min)
values.note: Earliest point a tank or witch can spawn on a middle map, as a share of the way through. First maps and finales use their own ranges, and many maps ban some stretches. Type !boss in game for the real spot.

values.label: Boss spawn flow (max)
values.note: Latest point a tank or witch can spawn on a middle map.

values.label: Saferoom lock on
values.note: Our lock: the end saferoom door is held open and cannot be closed while a boss is alive.

values.label: Uzi damage
values.note: Damage of one Uzi bullet at close range.

values.label: Uzi spread per shot
values.note: How much each shot widens the spread while you hold fire.

values.label: Uzi spread while moving
values.note: Widest the spread gets while moving.

values.label: Uzi range falloff
values.note: Share of damage a bullet keeps per 500 units of distance. Lower means damage falls off faster.

values.label: Boomer health
values.note: Boomer health.

values.label: Boomer speed
values.note: Boomer running speed.

values.label: Vomit duration
values.note: How long one vomit lasts.

values.label: Vomit speed
values.note: How fast the vomit travels.

values.label: Vomit fatigue
values.note: Slowdown a vomited survivor gets. Higher pins them in place longer.

values.label: Explosion bile radius
values.note: Survivors this close to a popping boomer get covered in bile.

values.label: Explosion force
values.note: How hard a popping boomer pushes survivors nearby.

values.label: Explosion inner radius
values.note: Survivors this close to a popping boomer take the full push.

values.label: Explosion outer radius
values.note: The push fades to nothing at this distance.

values.label: Boomer scratch damage
values.note: Damage of a boomer's scratch.

values.label: Hunter health
values.note: Hunter health.

values.label: Hunter speed
values.note: Hunter running speed.

values.label: Pounce power
values.note: Forward speed of a pounce.

values.label: Pounce lift
values.note: Upward push of a pounce.

values.label: DP: distance where extra damage starts
values.note: A pounce from farther than this starts doing extra damage on landing.

values.label: DP: distance for full damage
values.note: A pounce from this far or more does the full extra damage. Set by the max DP damage plugin.

values.label: Smoker health
values.note: Smoker health.

values.label: Smoker speed
values.note: Smoker running speed.

values.note: How far the tongue reaches.

values.label: Cooldown after a missed tongue
values.note: Cooldown after a tongue that misses.

values.note: How fast the tongue travels to its target.

values.note: A pulled survivor must be lifted this high off the ground to be choked in the air. A huge value turns that off.

values.label: Drag speed
values.note: Fastest a survivor is dragged.

values.label: Drop time after a tongue breaks
values.note: How long a tongue that missed or hit a wall waits before pulling back.

values.label: Smoker scratch damage
values.note: Damage of a smoker's scratch.

values.label: Time between punches
values.note: Shortest time between two tank punches.

values.label: Punch damage (versus)
values.note: Damage one tank punch does to a standing survivor in versus.

values.label: Rock throw force
values.note: How fast a thrown rock flies.

values.label: Rock hit radius
values.note: How close a rock must pass to a survivor to hit.

values.label: Time between rock throws
values.note: Shortest time between two rock throws.

values.label: Time for fire to kill a witch
values.note: A lit witch burns to death in this time. Molotovs and gas cans are removed in our PUG mode, so this mostly matters in Lite.

values.label: Witch startle range
values.note: Survivors this close to an angry witch make her attack.

values.label: Witch attack range
values.note: How close the witch has to be to slash.

values.label: Witch calm-down rate
values.note: How fast the witch calms down once survivors back off.

values.label: Common infected health
values.note: Health of a common infected.

values.label: Common infected speed
values.note: Running speed of common infected.

values.label: Pills give
values.note: Temporary health one bottle of pills gives.

values.label: Incapacitated health
values.note: Health you have while down. It bleeds out, and hitting 0 kills you.

values.label: Incapacitated health lost per second
values.note: How fast health bleeds away while you are down.

values.label: Limp below
values.note: Below this much health you limp and move slower.

values.label: Friendly fire damage factor
values.note: Share of normal damage your bullets deal to teammates. Versus runs on Normal difficulty, so this is the one that applies.

values.label: Crouch speed
values.note: Movement speed while crouched.

values.label: Fire damage factor
values.note: Share of fire damage survivors take. Versus runs on Normal difficulty, so this is the one that applies. Molotovs and gas cans are removed in our PUG mode, so this mostly matters in Lite.

values.label: Fire damage
values.note: Damage per second standing in fire, before the fire damage factor above. Molotovs and gas cans are removed in our PUG mode, so this mostly matters in Lite.

values.label: Fire duration
values.note: How long a molotov or gas can fire keeps burning. Molotovs and gas cans are removed in our PUG mode, so this mostly matters in Lite.

values.label: Ghost travel distance
values.note: A ghost this far from survivors along the map can spawn even if they are close in a straight line.

values.label: Minimum spawn distance from survivors
values.note: A ghost cannot spawn closer than this to any survivor.

values.label: Ghost speed
values.note: How fast a ghost moves.

values.label: Godframes after a pounce ends
values.note: How long a survivor cannot be hurt after being freed from a hunter.

values.label: Godframes after a smoker lets go
values.note: How long a survivor cannot be hurt after a smoker lets go.

values.label: Godframes after a revive
values.note: How long a survivor cannot be hurt after being picked up.

values.label: Extra time before commons can hurt
values.note: Common infected stay unable to hurt you for this much longer than the godframes above.

values.label: Extra time before friendly fire can hurt
values.note: Teammates stay unable to hurt you for this much longer than the godframes above.

values.label: Extra common protection applies after (1 hunter, 2 smoker, 4 revive)
values.note: Which releases get the extra common protection. Add up: 1 hunter, 2 smoker, 4 revive.

values.label: Extra friendly-fire protection applies after (1 hunter, 2 smoker, 4 revive)
values.note: Which releases get the extra friendly fire protection. Add up: 1 hunter, 2 smoker, 4 revive.

values.note: 1 means a hittable car or dumpster hurts you even during godframes.

values.label: Witch ignores godframes
values.note: 1 means the witch hurts you even during godframes.

values.label: Water run speed
values.note: Survivor top speed in water. Normal running speed is 220.

values.label: Water run speed during a tank
values.note: Survivor top speed in water while a tank is up. Normal running speed is 220.

values.label: Gunfire slowdown on special infected
values.note: How much gunfire slows special infected. 0 means not at all, 1 means the most.

values.label: Gunfire slowdown on the tank
values.note: How much gunfire slows the tank. 0 means not at all, 1 means the most.

values.label: Shove immunity after a hunter lands
values.note: For this long after a hunter lands, shoves cannot hit it.

values.label: Sky pounce: no-attack time
values.note: Mode 1: how long a hunter cannot attack in the air after such a pounce.

values.label: Sky pounce: angle from
values.note: Mode 1: the pounce has to start with the view angled down at least this much.

values.label: Sky pounce: angle to

values.label: Sky pounce: pounces off the sky per flight (mode 2)
values.note: Mode 2: pounces off the sky a hunter gets per flight.

values.label: Rage freeze: seconds per step

values.label: Get-up time after a punch (scale)

values.label: Shoves cannot kill hunters

values.note: Damage multiplier for a hunting rifle hit on a hunter's stomach.

rules.text: If the boomer dies last, the next wave is {sm_3ht1s_percent_chance}% likely to be 3 hunters + 1 smoker, otherwise 4 hunters.
Damage pounces (DPs): pounce damage grows with distance from {z_pounce_damage_range_min} units, up to {pounceuncap_maxdamage} damage at {z_pounce_damage_range_max} units or more.
Hunters cannot be deadstopped (shoved out of the air) mid-pounce, and cannot be shoved for {hunter_ground_m2_godframes} s after landing.

Sky pounce limit: a hunter that starts a pounce at a flat, ceiling-skimming angle ({l4d_skypounce_pitch_min} to {l4d_skypounce_pitch_max} degrees down) cannot attack again in the air for {l4d_skypounce_cooldown} s, which stops chaining pounces off the map's sky.
Sky pounce limit: a hunter can pounce off the map's sky {l4d_skypounce_allow} time per flight.

Godframes (survivors take no damage): {gfc_hunter_duration} s after a hunter's pounce ends, {gfc_smoker_duration} s after a smoker lets go, {gfc_revive_duration} s after a revive. After a smoker lets go, commons still cannot hurt for a further {gfc_common_extra_time} s and friendly fire for a further {gfc_ff_extra_time} s. Hittables and the witch always ignore godframes.

If survivors clear a tongue instantly, before it starts dragging or choking, the smoker's cooldown is {l4d_tongue_delay_survivor} s ({l4d_tongue_delay_tank} s if the tank clears it) instead of the normal {tongue_hit_delay} s.
Drag damage: {tongue_drag_first_damage} HP after the first {tongue_drag_first_damage_interval} s, then 1 HP every {tongue_drag_damage_interval} s.

Hunting rifle: fire rate x{l4d_huntingrifle_fire_rate}, {l4dbeta_huntingrifle_swtichtime} s switch time, {l4dbeta_huntingrifle_empty_reloadtime} s empty reload; {l4d_huntingrifle_tank_dmg} damage to the tank, x{l4d_huntingrifle_hunter_chest_multi} to a hunter's chest and x{l4d_huntingrifle_hunter_Stomach_multi} to its stomach.
Water slows survivors to {l4d_slowdown_water_survivors_run} ({l4d_slowdown_water_survivors_run_during_tank} while a tank is up). Gunfire does not slow special infected or the tank.

Anti-bait: once every infected player has been up (spawned or ghost) for {l4d_antibaiter_delay} s and the survivors are not moving forward, a {l4d_antibaiter_horde_timer} s countdown appears, and two hordes come when it runs out unless they move on. It does not run while a tank is alive or a panic event is on, and any infected death restarts it.

Tank rage freeze: when survivors run back, the tank's rage meter freezes for {l4d2_tankrage_freezetime} s for every {l4d2_tankrage_flowpercent}% of the map they retreat, so running back does not cost the tank control.

A tank rock can be shot out of the air once it is {sm_rock_godframes} s old. Shots count against a {sm_rock_hitbox_radius} unit sphere around the rock and are lag compensated, so shots that look like hits count.
Finales: no first finale tank and no tank on the escape run, so a finale has its usual tank earlier in the map and one tank once the finale starts.
Shoves cannot kill hunters or smokers.
Special infected cannot damage each other, except the tank. They can still scratch each other, which pushes them and can clear a smoker's pull.
Bunny hopping is blocked for survivors, smokers, boomers and the tank. Hunters can still bunny hop.
Pistols have a minimum time between shots: {l4d_pistol_delay_single} s, or {l4d_pistol_delay_dualies} s with dual pistols.
The end saferoom door is held open and cannot be closed while a tank or witch is alive.
Fire damage to the tank is capped at {l4d_tank_burn_cap} per round; then the fire goes out.
Pipe bombs and molotovs are removed from the map.
A chasing witch that makes no progress ({l4d_witch_unstuck_progress} units in {l4d_witch_unstuck_time} s) because she is stuck on the map is nudged free or hops past the obstacle.
Doors do not stumble the tank. In vanilla, shutting a door on a tank stumbles it for several seconds.
No health items on the map and no first aid kits. Every survivor is given one bottle of pills when each half goes live, and the finale has one extra bottle per survivor.

Health bonus: each survivor who reaches the saferoom scores half their health plus a quarter of their temporary health, plus {l4d_score_healthbounus_pill} for unused pills. A survivor who is down or hanging gets only the pills bonus. Type !bonus to check.
Press Reload while holding pills to pass them to a standing teammate who has none. A pass that fails comes back to you, and receiving pills does not switch your weapon.
Survivor bots never take pills. A player who takes over the bot gets them.
Rifles are replaced by Uzis and auto shotguns by pump shotguns. Hunting rifles stay on the map but cannot be picked up.

Reloading keeps the bullets already in your magazine. The new magazine counts after {l4d_smg_reload_clip_time} s (Uzi), {l4d_pistol_reload_clip_time} s (pistol) or {l4d_dualpistol_reload_clip_time} s (dual pistols), so you can cancel the rest of the animation.
No friendly fire from downed survivors, onto a survivor pinned by an infected, or at point-blank range. Uzi and pistol fire hurts the same teammate at most once every 0.3 s.
A survivor in godframes glows red.
A survivor who dies drops their pistol.
You can stand on another player's head, teammate or enemy, without sliding off. A pouncing hunter still slides.
Survivors do not push each other when standing close.
No heartbeat sound on black and white survivors and no downed pain sounds.
Survivors never shout "Hunter!" on their own.
A few seconds after a smoker or boomer spawns, a survivor says they hear it.

Hittables do fixed damage: 100 for cars, dumpsters and logs, less for small objects, the same to a downed survivor. One object cannot hit the same survivor twice within 1.4 s, and the tank is never hurt by its own hittables.
As a ghost, right-click jumps you to the next survivor, or type !warp with a number or name.
While staggered you cannot shoot, shove, scratch or pounce. This applies to both teams, except on ladders.
The infected team in the second half starts with the same classes the first half started with.
A survivor staying in the saferoom no longer gives the infected unlimited respawns.
Infected cannot see weapons or items on the map until a survivor has had them in view.
You cannot block an opponent climbing a ladder; standing on them bounces you off.
Tank rocks pass through commons and downed survivors, pulled survivors pass through commons, infected pass through the witch, and hunters pass through downed survivors.
Special infected can crouch and strafe while scratching.
If an infected player leaves, goes spectator or becomes the tank, their special infected dies instead of becoming a bot, unless it is pinning a survivor.
An infected player who goes spectator waits 10 s before they can rejoin the infected team.
Explosions from the map do not hurt special infected or the tank.
Being shot never stops a hunter from pouncing again.
Hunters can wall-kick off cars, dumpsters and other movable props.
A tongue passes through other infected (not the tank), and once fired it passes through survivors other than its target.
Shoving or staggering a smoker while its tongue is in flight cancels the shot.
A shoved boomer cannot vomit for 1 s.
Bile passes through other infected instead of being blocked by them.
Popping a boomer within {z_exploding_splat_radius} units of a witch that can see it startles her, and she goes for the shooter.
Panic events have no cooldown: an alarm right after a crescendo still triggers.
During panic events infected can spawn anywhere, not only ahead of the survivors, and commons can spawn in cleared areas.
Any survivor touching an alarm car sets it off, and a car hit by a tank hittable is disarmed. Bots do not trigger alarms.
Commons left far behind the last survivor, out of sight, are removed and respawned ahead.
Every map has one tank and one witch, except a few maps that have none.
Both teams meet the tank and the witch at the same point of the map, and they spawn in the same place.
The witch still spawns while a tank is alive.
Cars and objects the tank hits stay put while it lives, glow red for the infected, and disappear a few seconds after it dies.
A car or other big hittable that hits a survivor refills the tank's rage. Small ones only do if they incap.
Shoving the tank does nothing.
Tank attacks by button: M1 right hook, M1+E left hook, M1+R uppercut; M2 one-hand throw, E underhand, R two-hand overhead.
If your rage runs out and the tank goes to the AI, you wait the normal respawn timer.
After a rock hits you, you cannot revive or use anything for 1.5 s.
A newly spawned tank cannot be set on fire for its first few seconds.
When the rescue vehicle leaves, anyone down or hanging dies and does not score, and standing survivors take no more damage.
A startled witch follows you into the saferoom.
A shotgun blast that does 799 damage or more to the witch kills her outright.
The witch always uses the bride model.
Infected can spawn inside and break into the unused rescue closets.

Survivor bug fixes: no fall damage or health boost glitches, no temporary health exploits on ledges, no instant refill by picking up the same gun, a revive interrupts a reload properly, no fire damage glitch while down, shotgun pellets hit where they should, shove timing and shoves on commons fixed.
Exploit fixes: no ducking or ghost ducking exploits, no ammo pile refill trick, no pump shotgun fast-fire, no scratching while staggered.

Infected fixes: bot hunters can be skeeted like players, boomers no longer teleport near ladders, tongues do not bend around corners or leave survivors floating, ghosts cannot spawn in the start saferoom, commons do not get stuck on melee.

Tank fixes: no frozen tanks, punches do not get stuck or blocked, no falling punch glitch, rocks do not pass through black and white survivors, a tank cannot throw a rock by accident right after spawning.
Witch fixes: she does not lose her target, is not startled by doors, and does not freeze on corners.
Map fixes: doors behave while survivors are down, finale breakables and the escape route stay consistent between halves, and physics props push and touch correctly.
